newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper deplores infant's kidnapping.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper deplores infant's kidnapping.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper on Tuesday deplored the kidnapping of a newborn baby and said it underscored the need for psychiatrists in a country affected by "sick minds and souls."

"Only a peverse inclination toward evil could lead someone to think about and commit acts as monstrous as taking a mother's young son away from her before she even had a chance to caress him," Samper said in a speech marking the first anniversary of his government's anti-kidnapping task force.
He was referring to the weekend abduction from the tony Clinica del Country hospital in northern Bogota of 24-hour-old Juan Diego Saldana by a woman posing as a nurse.

Colombia has one of the highest kidnapping rates in the world. But the abduction of Juan Diego from his cradle grabbed front-page headlines in Bogota and prompted the National Police -- whose chief reiterated an earlier call on Tuesday for death sentences for kidnappers -- to offer a $30,000 for information leading to his safe return.
"This (crime) has led me to think that what some sectors of our society need is a psychiatrist, because they have sick minds and souls," Samper said.
"In the name of Juan Diego, I call on all kidnappers to release their captives and return them home."
